The [Hebrew alphabet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hebrew_alphabet) (often called the *alef-bet* after its first two letters) consists of **22 foundational letters** , all of which are consonants.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hebrew_alphabet)

### Key Features

- **Direction:** Written and read from **right to left**.
- **No Case:** There are no uppercase or lowercase distinctions.
- **Vowels (*Niqqud*):** Originally written as an abjad (consonants only). Vowel sounds are optionally indicated using a system of dots and dashes called *niqqud* placed above, below, or inside the letters.
- **Final Forms (*Sofit*):** Five letters change their shape when they appear at the very end of a word.
- **Numerical Values:** Each letter doubles as a number from 1 to 400 (used in *gematria* and everyday dating/numbering).[[1]](https://mena-languages.northwestern.edu/language-learning/languages-with-different-scripts/hebrew-alphabet.html)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hebrew_alphabet)[[3]](https://preply.com/en/blog/hebrew-alphabet-explained/)[[4]](https://zondervanacademic.com/blog/introduction-hebrew-alphabet)[[5]](https://jewishvirtuallibrary.org/the-hebrew-alphabet-aleph-bet)



---

### The 22 Letters in Order

1. **א** — Alef (silent)
2. **ב** — Bet / Vet (B or V sound)
3. **ג** — Gimel (G sound)
4. **ד** — Dalet (D sound)
5. **ה** — Heh (H sound / silent)
6. **ו** — Vav (V or O/U vowel sound)
7. **ז** — Zayin (Z sound)
8. **ח** — Chet / Khaf (throat H/Ch sound)
9. **ט** — Tet (T sound)
10. **י** — Yud (Y sound or I vowel)
11. **כ** *(Final form: **ך**)* — Kaf / Khaf (K or Ch sound)
12. **ל** — Lamed (L sound)
13. **מ** *(Final form: **ם**)* — Mem (M sound)
14. **נ** *(Final form: **ן**)* — Nun (N sound)
15. **ס** — Samekh (S sound)
16. **ע** — Ayin (silent / throat stop)
17. **פ** *(Final form: **ף**)* — Peh / Feh (P or F sound)
18. **צ** *(Final form: **ץ**)* — Tzadeh / Tzadik (Ts sound)
19. **ק** — Qof (K sound)
20. **ר** — Resh (R sound)
21. **ש** — Shin / Sin (Sh or S sound, depending on dot placement)
22. **ת** — Tav (T sound)[[1]](https://tcdecker.com/2026/05/10/the-hebrew-alphabet/)[[2]](https://zondervanacademic.com/blog/introduction-hebrew-alphabet)[[3]](https://www.lifeinmessiah.org/intro-to-the-hebrew-alphabet)[[4]](https://study.com/academy/lesson/hebrew-alphabet-overview-chart.html)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hebrew_alphabet)[[6]](https://elon.io/grammar/hebrew/pronunciation/letter-names)[[7]](https://www.chabad.org/library/article_cdo/aid/4069287/jewish/The-Hebrew-Alphabet.htm)[[8]](https://preply.com/en/blog/hebrew-alphabet-explained/)



---

### Writing Styles

- **Square / Block Script (*Ktav Ashurit*):** Used in printed books, newspapers, digital media, and Torah scrolls.
- **Cursive Script (*Ktav*):** A flowing, rounded handwritten script used for everyday notes and letters.[[1]](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/7uOHf3sIv3Y)[[2]](https://www.hebrew4christians.com/Grammar/Unit_One/Aleph-Bet/aleph-bet.html)[[3]](https://www.chabad.org/library/article_cdo/aid/4069287/jewish/The-Hebrew-Alphabet.htm)[[4]](https://mena-languages.northwestern.edu/language-learning/languages-with-different-scripts/hebrew-alphabet.html)
